text: The transport adds a null pair and climbs a tower without changing its residue. This note asks what a single added generator does to the oriented towers $\Cl(1,3)$ and $\Cl(3,1)$. A space-sign generator doubles the shadow, $\Cl(1,4) \cong \Cl(1,3) \oplus \Cl(1,3)$; a time-sign generator complexifies it, $\Cl(2,3) \cong \Cl(1,3) \otimes \C$, and there the mirror's algebra sits, on the anti-de Sitter translation bivectors. The first rung's even subalgebra is $\Cl(2,3)$, so the dark-matter paper's copy theorem runs inside the complexification that forgets the real form; the odd extension is the first construction above the shadow, by dimension, that keeps the towers apart, through an element no derived quantity uses. The dark-energy paper's frozen point realises the extension: its scale tractor and Stelle-West vector are the ascent's pair, signed by $\Lambda$, and the algebra of $I^{\perp}$ is the intermediate of this world's own ascent, $\Cl(1,4)$ for the observed $\Lambda > 0$, $\Cl(2,3)$ for $\Lambda < 0$, degenerate at $\Lambda = 0$. By the soldered residue that algebra is this tower's, so $\Lambda$ does not supply the coupling the dark towers need. Run on the degenerate case, the transport returns the rung and a canonical null frame and constrains the frozen point only through its norm: within the series $\Lambda$ is undetermined, its frame components are gauge, and its sign does not select the visible tower. The family over the $\Lambda$ line is a tame wall, completed on both sides in the case the sheaf paper's conservation theorem excludes. The note is a dictionary between three papers, with one new result and no prediction.

title: What a single generator does
Single extension
text: The \emph{time extension} of $\Cl(p,q)$ is $\Cl(p+1, q)$ and its \emph{space extension} is $\Cl(p, q+1)$, each with the new generator written $e_{n+1}$ and the old generators, and the subalgebra they generate, called the \emph{shadow}. A single extension is not a transport in the series' sense: the transport adjoins a null pair $e_{+} + e_{-}$ because a zero divisor of vector type is resolved by a nilpotent, and a single generator squaring to $\pm 1$ supplies none \cite[\S 8]{ButlerT1}.

title: The volume element in odd dimension
text: For $n$ odd, $\omega$ is central in $\Cl(p,q)$ and $\omega^{2} = (-1)^{n(n-1)/2 + q}$. For $n = 5$ this is $\omega^{2} = (-1)^{q}$.
proof: $e_{i}\omega = (-1)^{n-1}\omega e_{i}$ since $e_{i}$ anticommutes with the $n - 1$ other factors (\claimref{std-algebra.orthogonal-anticommute}) and commutes with itself; for $n$ odd the sign is $+1$, and the generators generate. Reversing the order of the $n$ factors costs $(-1)^{n(n-1)/2}$ and the contractions $e_{i}^{2}$ cost $(-1)^{q}$. The script verifies centrality and the sign on every diagonal signature of dimension one, three, five and seven.

title: Doubling or complexification
proof: (i) With $\omega$ central (Lemma \claimref{odd-extensions.volume-element-odd-dimension}) and $\omega^{2} = 1$ the elements $P_{\pm} = (1 \pm \omega)/2$ are central, idempotent, orthogonal and sum to one, so the algebra is the direct sum of the ideals $P_{\pm}\Cl$. The map $x \mapsto P_{\pm}x$ restricted to $\Cl^{0}$ is injective, since $\omega$ is odd and $x - \omega x$ can vanish for even $x$ only if $x = 0$, and surjective onto $P_{\pm}\Cl$ because $P_{\pm}y = P_{\pm}(y_{0} \pm \omega y_{1})$ for $y = y_{0} + y_{1}$ split by parity, with $\omega y_{1}$ even; and $P_{\pm}$ is central, so the map is an algebra isomorphism. Finally $\omega = \omega' e_{n}$ with $e_{n}$ commuting with $\omega'$ (it anticommutes with each of the $n - 1$ factors, an even number, \claimref{std-algebra.orthogonal-anticommute}), so $\omega^{2} = \omega'^{2}e_{n}^{2}$ and $\omega^{2} = 1$ forces $\omega'^{2} = e_{n}^{2} =: s \in \{\pm 1\}$; then $P_{\pm}\omega' = (\omega' \pm s\,e_{n})/2$ and $P_{\pm}e_{n} = (e_{n} \pm s\,\omega')/2 = \pm s\,P_{\pm}\omega'$, so $e_{n}$ acts on the two summands as $+s\,\omega'$ and $-s\,\omega'$. (ii) With $\omega^{2} = -1$ central, $\Cl$ is a $\C$-algebra through $\omega$, and the $\R$-linear map $\Cl^{0} \otimes \C \to \Cl$, $x \otimes (a + bi) \mapsto ax + b\,\omega x$, is an algebra homomorphism, injective by the parity argument, and surjective by dimension ($2 \cdot 2^{n-1} = 2^{n}$, \claimref{std-algebra.z2-grading}). (iii) For $e_{n}^{2} = -1$ the elements $e_{i}e_{n}$, $i < n$, anticommute pairwise and square to $-e_{i}^{2}e_{n}^{2} = e_{i}^{2}$, so they generate a copy of $\Cl(p,q)$ inside $\Cl^{0}(p, q+1)$, of the full dimension $2^{n-1}$; for $e_{n}^{2} = +1$ they square to $-e_{i}^{2}$ and generate $\Cl(q,p)$. The script verifies (iii), and the identities behind (i) and (ii) (the sign pairing $P_{\pm}e_{n} = \pm s P_{\pm}\omega'$, the dimensions and the spanning, but not the idempotent identities and not the algebra-map properties, which are argued above), over every odd signature of dimensions three and five, and (i) and (ii) in detail on the four extensions of Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.four-extensions-oriented-pair}: the idempotents, the two ideals of dimension sixteen, the action of $e_{5}$ as $\pm\omega'$ on them, and the spanning of all thirty-two dimensions by $\Cl(p,q) + \omega\,\Cl(p,q)$ in the complexified cases.

title: The four extensions of the oriented pair
text:
The single extensions of this world and its mirror are, with their residues,
\[
\begin{array}{lllll}
\toprule
\text{extension} & \text{algebra} & \omega^{2} & \text{structure} & r \\
\midrule
\text{this world} + \text{space} & \Cl(1,4) & +1 & \Cl(1,3) \oplus \Cl(1,3) & 5 \\
\text{this world} + \text{time}  & \Cl(2,3) & -1 & \Cl(1,3) \otimes \C \cong \Mat(4,\C), \ \Cl^{0} \cong \Cl(3,1) & 7 \\
\text{mirror} + \text{space}     & \Cl(3,2) & +1 & \Cl(3,1) \oplus \Cl(3,1) & 1 \\
\text{mirror} + \text{time}      & \Cl(4,1) & -1 & \Cl(3,1) \otimes \C \cong \Mat(4,\C), \ \Cl^{0} \cong \Cl(1,3) & 3 \\
\bottomrule
\end{array}
\]
In both towers the generator of the time sign complexifies and the generator of the space sign doubles. The labels follow the uniform convention (time a generator of square $+1$, space one of square $-1$, in both towers); in T14's causal convention the mirror's time is its minus sign, so its space and time extensions are $\Cl(4,1)$ and $\Cl(3,2)$, each the reversal of ours of the same kind, and the convention-free rule is that a generator of square $-1$ doubles and one of square $+1$ complexifies (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.mirror-extensions-causal-convention}).
proof: Both shadows have $q$ odd ($3$ and $1$); a time generator leaves $q$ unchanged and a space generator raises it by one, so by Lemma \claimref{odd-extensions.volume-element-odd-dimension} the time extensions have $\omega^{2} = -1$ and the space extensions $\omega^{2} = +1$, and Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.doubling-or-complexification} gives the structures. The even subalgebras are from Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.doubling-or-complexification}(iii): $\Cl^{0}(1,4) \cong \Cl(1,3)$, $\Cl^{0}(2,3) \cong \Cl(3,1)$, $\Cl^{0}(3,2) \cong \Cl(3,1)$, $\Cl^{0}(4,1) \cong \Cl(1,3)$. The residues are $p - q \bmod 8$. The identification $\Cl(1,3) \otimes \C \cong \Mat(4,\C)$ (\claimref{std-algebra.sta-matrix}) is Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-representatives-dimension-nearest-four-types} complexified.

title: the added axis is the pseudoscalar
text: In the doubled case the fifth generator is nothing new: on each summand it acts as the pseudoscalar $\omega' = e_{1}e_{2}e_{3}e_{4}$ of the shadow, up to sign, so the extra space direction of $\Cl(1,4)$ is the chirality operator of $\Cl(1,3)$ promoted from a $4$-blade to a vector, with the choice of sign the only datum the extension adds. In the complexified case the fifth generator is $e_{5} = \pm\,\omega\,\omega'^{-1}$, that is $i\gamma_{5}$ in the physicists' notation, and the algebra is the complexified Dirac algebra.

title: Where the mirror sits
The mirror inside the complexified extension, and absent from the doubled one
proof:
(i) is the definition of the shadow. (ii) is Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.doubling-or-complexification}(iii) with $e_{5}^{2} = +1$: the products square to $-e_{\mu}^{2}$, which is $(-1, +1, +1, +1)$, and generate a subalgebra of dimension sixteen inside the even subalgebra of dimension sixteen. (iii) The shadow's even part consists of even elements of $\Cl(2,3)$, so it lies in the intersection; the shadow's odd part consists of odd elements of $\Cl(2,3)$, since the generators $e_{1}, \ldots, e_{4}$ are odd there, so it meets the even subalgebra in zero; the intersection is exactly $\Cl^{0}(1,3)$, of dimension eight, and $\Cl^{0}(1,3) \cong \Cl(3,0)$ (\claimref{std-algebra.sta-matrix}) $\cong \Mat(2,\C)$ (\claimref{std-algebra.pauli-algebra}) is the Pauli algebra. For the spanning statement: $\omega$ times a blade of the shadow is, up to sign, the complementary blade of the shadow times $e_{5}$, so $\Cl(1,3) + \omega\,\Cl(1,3)$ contains every blade of $\Cl(2,3)$ (the script checks the dimension); this is the shadow's version of Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.doubling-or-complexification}(ii), which decomposes by the even subalgebra instead. (iv) An automorphism carries a subalgebra to an isomorphic subalgebra, and $\Cl(1,3) \not\cong \Cl(3,1)$ by Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-representatives-dimension-nearest-four-types}. With $\omega$ central and $\omega^{2} = -1$, $(\omega e_{\mu})^{2} = -e_{\mu}^{2}$ and the $\omega e_{\mu}$ anticommute pairwise, so they generate a $\Cl(3,1)$; this is the complex-linear identification of the two real forms and it is not an automorphism of the real algebra, since $\omega e_{\mu}$ is a $4$-blade, not a vector.

For $\Cl(1,4)$: Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.doubling-or-complexification}(iii) with $e_{5}^{2} = -1$ gives $(e_{\mu}e_{5})^{2} = e_{\mu}^{2}$, and $\omega^{2} = +1$ gives $(\omega e_{\mu})^{2} = e_{\mu}^{2}$, so all three sets generate $\Cl(1,3)$. For the non-embedding: $\Cl(1,4) \cong A \oplus A$ with $A = \Cl(1,3) \cong \Mat(2,\HH)$ by Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.doubling-or-complexification}(i) and Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-representatives-dimension-nearest-four-types}. A unital homomorphism $\phi: \Mat(4,\R) \to A \oplus A$ composed with the projection to a summand on which $\phi(1) \neq 0$ is a unital homomorphism $\Mat(4,\R) \to A$; its kernel is a two-sided ideal of the simple algebra $\Mat(4,\R)$ not containing $1$, hence zero; so it is injective between real algebras of equal dimension sixteen, hence an isomorphism, contradicting $\Mat(4,\R) \not\cong \Mat(2,\HH)$ (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-representatives-dimension-nearest-four-types}). The statements for the mirror's extensions follow by exchanging the roles of $p$ and $q$ throughout. The script verifies the squares, the anticommutation, the dimensions of the generated subalgebras and of their intersections with the even subalgebra, and the Wick-rotated squares, for all four extensions.

title: The translation bivectors of the frozen point
proof: Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point} gives the signature of $I^{\perp}$ as $(1,4)$ or $(2,3)$ by the sign of $\Lambda$, the sign of $Q(V) = -3/\Lambda$, and $\{I,V\}^{\perp}$ of signature $(1,3)$ in both cases; so $e_{5}^{2} = \operatorname{sign}Q(V)$ is $-1$ for $\Lambda > 0$ and $+1$ for $\Lambda < 0$, and $\Cl(I^{\perp})$ is the space extension or the time extension of $\Cl(1,3)$ respectively. The translation part of the reduced connection is $e^{\mu}\wedge V/\ell$, whose Clifford image is the bivector $e_{\mu}e_{5}$ up to the scalar $1/\ell$; the algebra these generate is Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.mirror-inside-complexified-extension-absent-doubled}: $\Cl(1,3)$ in the first case, $\Cl(3,1)$ in the second. The contraction rescales the generators by $1/\ell$ and rescaling does not change the signs of the squares.

title: what this says, and what it does not
text: The de Sitter algebra of this world is two copies of this world, and the anti-de Sitter algebra of this world is this world merged with its mirror, with the mirror sitting on the momenta. This is a statement about the fibrewise Clifford algebra of $I^{\perp}$, which Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point} supplies; it is not a statement that a negative cosmological constant would turn matter into mirror matter. The tower charge is soldered and superselected (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-copy-theorem-soldered-residue}), and Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.every-path-mirror-crosses-two-time} below shows that no path of sign changes at fixed dimension four connects the two oriented towers without passing through a sterile signature. What the proposition does establish is that the sign of $\Lambda$ selects which of two non-isomorphic algebras the frozen point's translation generators live in, and that only one of them contains the mirror. The observed cosmological constant is positive \cite{Planck2018}, so the algebra realised in this universe is the doubled $\Cl(1,4)$ with no copy of the mirror in it; the mirror on the momenta is a statement about the other sign. The same source gives the present Hubble rate as exceeding the asymptotic rate $\sqrt{\Lambda/3}$ of Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.exceptional-algebra-residue-completion-both-sides}(ii) by the factor $\Omega_{\Lambda}^{-1/2}$.

title: The rung's even subalgebra is the anti-de Sitter algebra
The even conformal algebra is $\Cl(2,3)$
proof: (i) Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.doubling-or-complexification}(iii) applied to $\Cl(2,4)$ with a spacelike distinguished generator gives $\Cl^{0}(2,4) \cong \Cl(2,3)$, and with a timelike one $\Cl^{0}(2,4) \cong \Cl(4,1)$; both are $\Mat(4,\C)$ by Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.four-extensions-oriented-pair}. For $n = 6$ even, $\omega_{6}$ anticommutes with every vector, hence commutes with every even element, and $\omega_{6}^{2} = (-1)^{15}(-1)^{4} = -1$ (\claimref{std-algebra.pseudoscalar-commutation}, \claimref{primer.sign}); being even it lies in $\Cl^{0}(2,4)$ and is central there, and since $\Cl^{0}(2,4) \cong \Mat(4,\C)$ has centre $\C$, $\omega_{6}$ is the complex unit up to sign. (ii) The squares are $(e_{i}e_{6})^{2} = -e_{i}^{2}e_{6}^{2} = e_{i}^{2} = (1, -1, -1, -1)$ for $i = 2, \ldots, 5$ with the signature $(+,+,-,-,-,-)$, and $(e_{i}e_{1})^{2} = -e_{i}^{2} = (-1, 1, 1, 1)$; both sets anticommute pairwise and generate subalgebras of dimension sixteen. (iii) The conformal spin group is generated by the bivectors of $\Cl(2,4)$, which are even, and acts on $\CS$ through $\Cl^{0}(2,4)$ (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-conformal-completion}); the conformal spinor space $\CS \cong \C^{4}$ (twistor space) is the irreducible module of $\Cl^{0}(2,4) \cong \Mat(4,\C)$; the isotropic structure is a structure on $V_{\C} = \C^{6}$, the complexification of the ambient; and the mass formula is a bivector norm in the even subalgebra. (iv) An isomorphism of algebras restricts to an isomorphism of centres; the centre of an odd Clifford algebra is spanned by $1$ and $\omega$: a basis blade commutes with $e_{i}$ exactly when $e_{i}$ anticommutes with an even number of its factors, which for a blade of grade $k$ containing $e_{i}$ requires $k - 1$ even and for one not containing it requires $k$ even, and only the scalar and the volume element satisfy both conditions for every $i$; since $x \mapsto e_{i}xe_{i}^{-1}$ is diagonal in the blade basis, an element commutes with every $e_{i}$ exactly when each of its blades does, so the centre is spanned by those two (the script confirms dimension two over every odd signature of dimension at most five, and dimension one over every even signature of dimension at most six), and is $\R \oplus \R$ when $\omega^{2} = +1$ and $\C$ when $\omega^{2} = -1$; Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.four-extensions-oriented-pair} gives the signs. The script verifies (i), (ii) and the centre dimensions.

title: The copy theorem's blind spot
text: The copy theorem identifies this world and its mirror by working in an algebra, $\Cl^{0}(2,4) \cong \Cl(2,3)$, that contains both real forms and is the complexification of each, its complex unit being the conformal pseudoscalar $I_6$ that spans its centre with $1$. It is therefore exactly blind to the distinction that a single extension sees: the two oriented towers have isomorphic conformal spin groups, isomorphic conformal spinor modules (twistor modules) and one complexified ambient, but odd extensions that signature reversal does not identify (Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.twistor-algebra}(iv)), whose centres differ. The shadows themselves are non-isomorphic (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-representatives-dimension-nearest-four-types}); every object the copy theorem is built from, the even subalgebra of the rung, the conformal spin group and the conformal spinor module $\CS$ (Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.twistor-algebra}(iii)), identifies the two towers, while the rungs themselves, $\Cl(2,4)$ and $\Cl(4,2)$, do not, being of the two towers' types by Facts \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-towers-clock} and \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-representatives-dimension-nearest-four-types}; the odd extension is the first construction above the shadow, by dimension, that keeps them apart, and it does so through an element, the bare fifth generator, that no derived quantity of the series uses (Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.two-towers-one-curved-universe}).
proof: Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.twistor-algebra}(iii) and (iv). The remaining clauses rest on Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-representatives-dimension-nearest-four-types}, which supplies the non-isomorphic shadow types $\Cl(1,3) \cong \Mat(2,\HH)$ and $\Cl(3,1) \cong \Mat(4,\R)$; on Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-towers-clock}, whose $(1,1)$ ascent preserves the residue and so gives the rungs the two towers' types; and on Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.two-towers-one-curved-universe}, which supplies that the element distinguishing the two towers' intermediate algebras is one no derived quantity of the series uses.

title: the holographic coincidence
text: Writing, as here, $\Cl(2,4)$ for the Clifford algebra of the flat space in which $\mathrm{AdS}_{5}$ is the hyperboloid, and likewise for the other hyperboloids: the rung is the algebra of $\mathrm{AdS}_{5}$, whose isometry group $SO(2,4)$ is the conformal group of this world; the intermediate $\Cl(2,3)$ is the algebra of $\mathrm{AdS}_{4}$ and, by Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.four-extensions-are-four-odd-towers}, the conformal ambient of the three-dimensional residue-$7$ shadow, the group theory of $\mathrm{AdS}_{4}/\mathrm{CFT}_{3}$; the de Sitter intermediate $\Cl(1,4)$ is the ambient of the Euclidean three-dimensional shadow $(0,3)$, also of residue $5$, the group theory of $\mathrm{dS}/\mathrm{CFT}$. All of this is the standard fact that the isometry group of $\mathrm{AdS}_{d+1}$ is the conformal group in $d$ dimensions, which any conformal field theory in $d$ dimensions shares whether or not a bulk exists; the note adds only the residues. The coincidence does expose a difference in what two frameworks say about one pair of algebras. Holography takes the bulk and its boundary to be one physics in two descriptions. The series takes the residue of a sector to be the signature of its soldered space (Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.belongs-tower}), which a conformal class carries as well as a metric, so the boundary of $\mathrm{AdS}_{4}$ has residue $7$ and lies, by Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-towers-clock}, in a tower distinct from the bulk's; whether a conformal class with no chosen scale is also a superselected sector, Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-copy-theorem-soldered-residue} speaking of the one metric, is a separate question and is not settled here; and the series' superselection is a statement about operators soldered to one metric, which a holographic dictionary is not. Whether that last difference means the two frameworks are speaking about different things, or that one of them is wrong about this pair, is not argued anywhere in the series and is not argued here; the remark records the question and claims nothing about the dynamical content of holography, to which the series has no counterpart.

title: The clock, and the paths between the oriented towers
The four extensions are the four odd towers
text: The residues of the four extensions are $5$, $7$, $1$, $3$ (Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.four-extensions-oriented-pair}), and they land on the odd towers in two roles: $\Cl(1,4)$ and $\Cl(4,1)$, this world's space extension and the mirror's time extension, are the representatives at the dimension nearest four of the residues $5$ and $3$ (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-representatives-dimension-nearest-four-types}), the two five-dimensional dark towers; $\Cl(2,3)$ and $\Cl(3,2)$, this world's time extension and the mirror's space extension, are the conformal ambients (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-conformal-completion}) of the representatives $(1,2)$ and $(2,1)$ of the residues $7$ and $1$, the two three-dimensional dark towers. This is a statement about abstract algebras: the frozen point's algebra $\Cl(I^{\perp})$ of Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.translation-bivectors-frozen-point} coincides with a five-dimensional shadow for $\Lambda > 0$ and with a three-dimensional ambient for $\Lambda < 0$ as an algebra, and Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.belongs-tower} says that as a soldered object it is neither.
proof: $(1,4)$ and $(4,1)$, the space and time extensions of Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.four-extensions-oriented-pair}, are listed in Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-representatives-dimension-nearest-four-types} at $r = 5$ and $r = 3$. The conformal completion (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-conformal-completion}) of $(1,2)$ is $(2,3)$ and of $(2,1)$ is $(3,2)$, residues $7$ and $1$, preserved by the $(1,1)$ step (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-towers-clock}). The last sentence is Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.translation-bivectors-frozen-point} read against the first two, with Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.belongs-tower} for the soldering. The script checks every residue.

title: Every path to the mirror crosses the two-time fork
text: At fixed dimension four, a change of the sign of one generator moves the signature $(p, 4-p)$ to $(p \pm 1, 4 - p \mp 1)$ and the residue by $\pm 2$. Every sequence of such changes from $(1,3)$ to $(3,1)$ passes through $(2,2)$, residue $0$, the two-time sterile fork; the other neighbour of $(1,3)$, the Euclidean $(0,4)$ at residue $4$, is a dead end from which the only continuation returns to $(1,3)$.
proof: The signatures at dimension four are the five points $p = 0, \ldots, 4$ on a line, a sign change moves $p$ by one, and a walk from $p = 1$ to $p = 3$ visits $p = 2$; $p = 0$ has one neighbour. The script enumerates every non-revisiting walk of length at most six and finds exactly one, $(1,3) \to (2,2) \to (3,1)$.

title: no mechanism
text: Together with Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-copy-theorem-soldered-residue} this closes the question of a physical passage between the oriented towers within the series: the tower charge is superselected by the one metric, the only algebra in which both towers are present identifies them by the complex unit and not by any automorphism (Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.mirror-inside-complexified-extension-absent-doubled}(iv)), and the only continuous route through signatures at dimension four runs through a signature with no causal structure. The two towers share gravity, and by Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.translation-bivectors-frozen-point} the sign of $\Lambda$; that is the whole of the shared channel.

title: The frozen point splits the ascent's pair
The frozen point splits the ascent's pair
text: The rung of this world is $\Cl(2,4)$, obtained from $\Cl(1,3)$ by adjoining a hyperbolic pair, one generator of each sign, whose null combinations are the zero divisors the transport resolves (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-towers-clock}, Definition \claimref{obj.odd-extensions.single-extension}). The frozen point of the dark-energy paper is a vector in that rung, and its norm is the cosmological constant. This section shows that $I$ and the Stelle-West vector $V$ are the ascent's pair, signed by $\Lambda$, and that the odd extensions of the section ``What a single generator does'' are the intermediate algebras of this world's own ascent, with the degenerate case at $\Lambda = 0$ the wall of the sheaf paper.

title: Imported: the frozen point at $\Lambda = 0$, and the degenerate algebras
text: At $\Lambda = 0$ the parallel scale tractor is null, its stabiliser is parabolic (the Poincar\'e-type stabiliser of a null direction), and the rotation to the reductive de Sitter stabiliser happens exactly when $Q(I) \neq 0$; the identity $Q(I)\,Q(V) = -1$ holds for $\Lambda \neq 0$. A quadratic space with a one-dimensional radical has Clifford algebra $\Cl(p,q;1)$ with a nilpotent generator $n$, $n^{2} = 0$, and $n\,\Cl(p,q;1)$ is a two-sided ideal of square zero; the series treats these algebras, their nilpotent ideals and their one-sided completions in the sheaf paper, and a nilpotent generator is the vector-type zero divisor whose resolution is the transport. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Fact~2.1, Thm.~3.1]{ButlerT10}; \cite[Thm.~3.1, Prop.~3.4, Thm.~4.4]{ButlerT4}; \cite[\S 4]{ButlerT1}.
proof: At $\Lambda = 0$ the parallel scale tractor is null, its stabiliser is parabolic (the Poincar\'e-type stabiliser of a null direction), and the rotation to the reductive de Sitter stabiliser happens exactly when $Q(I) \neq 0$; the identity $Q(I)\,Q(V) = -1$ holds for $\Lambda \neq 0$. A quadratic space with a one-dimensional radical has Clifford algebra $\Cl(p,q;1)$ with a nilpotent generator $n$, $n^{2} = 0$, and $n\,\Cl(p,q;1)$ is a two-sided ideal of square zero; the series treats these algebras, their nilpotent ideals and their one-sided completions in the sheaf paper, and a nilpotent generator is the vector-type zero divisor whose resolution is the transport. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Fact~2.1, Thm.~3.1]{ButlerT10} (\claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}, \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry}); \cite[Thm.~3.1, Prop.~3.4, Thm.~4.4]{ButlerT4} (\claimref{sheaf.degeneration-sheaf}, \claimref{sheaf.resolution-ideal-theoretically}, \claimref{sheaf.one-sided-completion}); \cite[\S 4]{ButlerT1}.

title: $I$ and $V$ are the ascent's pair, signed by $\Lambda$
proof: Write the rung's hyperbolic plane orthogonal to the Lorentz frame as $\mathrm{span}(e_{+}, e_{-})$ with $e_{+}^{2} = +1$, $e_{-}^{2} = -1$; the frozen point is $I = c\,e_{+} + d\,e_{-}$ with $c^{2} - d^{2} = \Lambda/3$, and the orthogonal vector in the plane is $w = d\,e_{+} + c\,e_{-}$ with $Q(w) = d^{2} - c^{2} = -Q(I)$ and $\ip{I}{w} = cd - cd = 0$. (i) For $\Lambda \neq 0$, $V$ is the section of $I^{\perp}$ of norm $-3/\Lambda$ orthogonal to the Lorentz frame (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point}), so $V$ is a multiple of $w$ and $Q(I)\,Q(V) < 0$ is the identity of Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point-degenerate-algebras}. Orthogonal vectors anticommute in a Clifford algebra. (ii) $I^{\perp} = \{I,V\}^{\perp} \oplus \mathrm{span}(w)$ by dimension, and $e_{V}^{2} = \operatorname{sign}Q(V) = -\operatorname{sign}\Lambda$; so the five generators have signature $(1,3) + (0,1) = (1,4)$ for $\Lambda > 0$ and $(1,3) + (1,0) = (2,3)$ for $\Lambda < 0$, which are the two extensions of Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.four-extensions-oriented-pair}. The five together with $e_{I}$ are an orthogonal basis of the rung's vector space, so they generate $\Cl(2,4)$. (iii) At $c = d$, $Q(I) = 0$ and $w = I$, so $I \in I^{\perp}$, the induced form has the one-dimensional radical $\mathrm{span}(I)$, and the Clifford algebra of the five generators has one null generator: $\Cl(1,3;1)$, with the ideal and its square as in Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point-degenerate-algebras}. (iv) The Lorentz frame is orthogonal to both $e_{+}$ and $e_{-}$ and its signature does not depend on $c, d$. The script verifies (i) to (iv) on exact rational instances with $Q(I) = 3$, $-3$ and $0$: the orthogonality relations, the signatures $(1,4)$, $(2,3)$ and $(1,3;1)$ by exact congruence, the anticommutation, the generation of all sixty-four dimensions when $Q(I) \neq 0$, the nilpotent generator and its ideal in $\Cl(1,3;1)$, and the signature $(1,3)$ of the Lorentz frame in all three cases.

title: The cosmological constant deforms the wall
text: The intermediate algebra of this world's ascent is a one-parameter family in $\Lambda$: the degenerate $\Cl(1,3;1)$ at $\Lambda = 0$, whose nilpotent generator is the zero divisor the transport is built to resolve, deformed to the doubled $\Cl(1,4)$ for $\Lambda > 0$ and the complexified $\Cl(2,3)$ for $\Lambda < 0$. The sign of $\Lambda$ fixes the sign given to the ascent's null generator (the generator's square is $-\Lambda/3$, the opposite sign), and the two odd extensions are the two ways of giving it one.
proof: Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed}(ii) and (iii); the family is $I = c\,e_{+} + d\,e_{-}$ with $c^{2} - d^{2} = \Lambda/3$.

title: what this adds to the dark-energy paper
text: The dark-energy paper proves the parabolic-to-reductive rotation of the stabiliser at $\Lambda \neq 0$ at the level of groups. Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed} is the same rotation at the level of the Clifford algebra: the null direction of the parabolic case is the nilpotent generator of a degenerate algebra, and the reductive case is that generator given a sign. That the tangent image keeps signature $(1,3)$ whatever $\Lambda$ does is Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed}(iv) read through Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-copy-theorem-soldered-residue}.

title: The soldering decides
The soldering decides
text: the section ``The clock, and the paths between the oriented towers'' placed the four extensions on the four odd towers as algebras. The dark-matter paper's definition of the residue is not algebraic, and applying it settles which tower the frozen point's algebra belongs to.

title: $\Cl(I^{\perp})$ belongs to this tower
proof: (i) is Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point} with Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed}(iv). (ii) The residue is the signature of the soldered space by definition (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-copy-theorem-soldered-residue}), and that signature is $(1,3)$, residue $6$; the algebra generated by the soldered space together with the unsoldered $e_{V}$ lies inside the rung generated by the soldered space together with the ascent's pair. (iii) A five-dimensional shadow of residue $5$ is, by the same definition, an algebra whose soldered space has signature $(1,4)$, so all five generators are tangent; under the one four-dimensional metric of the dark-matter paper's Premise P1 (\claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point}) this needs a fifth tangent direction beyond the four, an internal direction in the sense of that paper's projection lemma \cite[Lem.~6.1]{ButlerT14} (\claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones}). The isometry $I^{\perp} \cong \R^{1,4}$ identifies $e_{V}$ with that direction, so it does not carry the soldered space onto the soldered space, which is what the dark-matter paper's Theorem 3.5(i) requires of a map that preserves the residue.

title: The two readings, and which is which
text: The two readings of $\Cl(1,4)$ that occur in the series are two solderings of one algebra, and the series' definition of the residue assigns them to different towers. The fifth direction of the frozen point's algebra is not a spacetime direction and never was: it is the Stelle-West vector, the normal to the de Sitter hyperboloid, with fixed norm $\ell = \sqrt{3/\Lambda}$, and its algebra is this tower's. The five-dimensional dark towers, if populated, are soldered to a fifth tangent direction that the frozen point does not supply, whose size $L$ remains the datum the series does not fix. Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.four-extensions-are-four-odd-towers} therefore holds as a statement about algebras, and only about algebras.
proof: Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.belongs-tower}.

title: $\Lambda$ is not a coupling between towers
text: The cosmological constant is a datum of this tower's ascent (Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed}), and its coincidence with the residue-$5$ tower's abstract algebra carries no structure across the superselection, since the dark-matter paper's exactness argument is precisely that isomorphisms between towers that do not respect the soldering carry nothing (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-copy-theorem-soldered-residue}). The coupling rule the dark-matter paper's odd towers need is not supplied by $\Lambda$.
proof: Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.belongs-tower}(iii) and Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-copy-theorem-soldered-residue}. The first sentence rests on Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed}, which supplies $\Lambda$ as a datum of this tower's ascent, the sign of $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$ on the ascent's pair.

title: what the copies are
text: the section ``What a single generator does'' to the section ``The rung's even subalgebra is the anti-de Sitter algebra'' are about this world's own ascent. The copy of the mirror's algebra that Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.translation-bivectors-frozen-point}(ii) finds on the translation bivectors for $\Lambda < 0$ is not the mirror tower, whose vectors are soldered; it is the reason the two oriented towers' intermediate algebras are non-isomorphic (Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.copy-theorems-blind-spot}), and that non-isomorphism is a statement about the two towers' own ascents under their own solderings, unaffected by this section. Likewise the odd towers' algebras that Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.four-extensions-are-four-odd-towers} finds among the four extensions are their abstract algebras only.

title: Running the transport on the wall
Running the transport on the wall
text: the section ``The frozen point splits the ascent's pair'' put the frozen point at $\Lambda = 0$ on the wall: the nilpotent generator of $\Cl(1,3;1)$. The series has a procedure for walls, the transport, and this section runs it and asks what it fixes and what it leaves free. The answer is that it fixes the rung and a canonical null frame in the rung's new plane, and nothing about the frozen point's position in that plane beyond what its norm, the cosmological constant, records.

title: Imported: the minimal completion of a degenerate algebra, and Rule 1
text: A real quadratic space with nondegenerate part of signature $(p,q)$ and radical of dimension $r$ admits a nondegenerate completion; every completion has dimension at least $p + q + 2r$; the minimal ones have signature exactly $(p+r, q+r)$; and any two minimal completions are isometric by an isometry fixing the original space pointwise, so the minimal ambient Clifford algebra $\Cl(p+r, q+r)$ is unique up to an isomorphism fixing the embedded $\Cl(p,q;r)$. In the model completion the radical is paired with its dual, $Q(\rho, \varphi) = 1$, $Q(\varphi,\varphi) = 0$, $\varphi$ orthogonal to the nondegenerate part. For a type-N obstruction in a nondegenerate algebra the increment $(+1,+1)$ is forced outright; for a type-C obstruction the completed algebra is unique but the sign of the adjoined generator's square is a geometric datum the algebra forgets. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Thm.~2.3 and its model]{ButlerT2}; \cite[Thm.~4.13, Thm.~5.7 and Rem.~5.8]{ButlerT1}.
proof: A real quadratic space with nondegenerate part of signature $(p,q)$ and radical of dimension $r$ admits a nondegenerate completion; every completion has dimension at least $p + q + 2r$; the minimal ones have signature exactly $(p+r, q+r)$; and any two minimal completions are isometric by an isometry fixing the original space pointwise, so the minimal ambient Clifford algebra $\Cl(p+r, q+r)$ is unique up to an isomorphism fixing the embedded $\Cl(p,q;r)$. In the model completion the radical is paired with its dual, $Q(\rho, \varphi) = 1$, $Q(\varphi,\varphi) = 0$, $\varphi$ orthogonal to the nondegenerate part. For a type-N obstruction in a nondegenerate algebra the increment $(+1,+1)$ is forced outright; for a type-C obstruction the completed algebra is unique but the sign of the adjoined generator's square is a geometric datum the algebra forgets. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Thm.~2.3 and its model]{ButlerT2} (\claimref{conformal.minimal-nondegenerate-completion}); \cite[Thm.~4.13, Thm.~5.7 and Rem.~5.8]{ButlerT1} (\claimref{transport.minimality}, \claimref{transport.one-generator-minimal-minimal-completions-classified}).

title: The transport constrains the frozen point only through its norm
proof: (i) Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-minimal-completion-degenerate-algebra-rule} with $(p,q,r) = (1,3,1)$ gives $(2,4)$. An isometry of $\widetilde W$ fixing $W$ pointwise sends $\varphi$ to a vector $x$ with $Q(x, w) = Q(\varphi, w)$ for all $w \in W$ and $Q(x,x) = 0$; the five linear conditions have rank five in six unknowns, so $x = \varphi + cI$, and $Q(x,x) = 2c\,Q(I,\varphi) = 2c$ forces $c = 0$. (ii) $Q(aI + b\varphi, aI + b\varphi) = 2ab\,Q(I,\varphi) = 2ab$; the vector is orthogonal to the Lorentz frame because $I$ and $\varphi$ are. (iii) The plane $\mathrm{span}(I,\varphi)$ is the orthogonal complement of the Lorentz frame, so an isometry fixing the frame restricts to an isometry of the plane, and the isometry group of a hyperbolic plane is $O(1,1)$: the boosts $(a,b) \mapsto (ta, b/t)$, $t > 0$, the swap $(a,b) \mapsto (b,a)$, and their products with $-1$. The boosts are transitive on each branch of each hyperbola $2ab = \text{const} \neq 0$ and on each of the four null rays; the element $-1$ exchanges the two branches of a hyperbola, and the swap exchanges the two null axes; so the orbits are the level sets of the norm. (iv) Isometries preserve the norm; the non-isomorphism is Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.twistor-algebra}(iv). The script verifies the signature, the rank-five linear system and its unique null solution, the norm formula on instances of both signs and zero, the boost and swap invariances, and the centres.

title: The cosmological constant is undetermined within the series
text: The transport, run on the wall, returns the rung and a canonical null frame in its new plane, and stops; the frozen point's position in that plane is data the transport receives, not data it produces, and the one invariant of that position is the norm $\Lambda/3$, sign and magnitude together. Within the series the sign is a choice between two options that the construction makes inequivalent (Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.transport-constrains-frozen-point-only-through}(iv)) and that nothing in the construction decides, which is the status the dark-matter paper's Premise P2 gives to the choice of which oriented tower is the visible one; the analogy is one of status, since P2's choice is binary and this one is a real modulus. Nothing here says the sign has no cause: only that the transport is not it.
proof: Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.transport-constrains-frozen-point-only-through}(iii) and (iv), with \cite[Premise P2]{ButlerT14} for the status.

title: the dictionary with the ascent's null pair
text:
The correspondence between the frozen point and the pair the transport adjoins, stated in the root paper's normalisation (which fixes the null basis up to the dilation, one hyperbolic plane being isometric to any other). The adjoined plane has the signed basis $e_{\pm}$ and the null basis $v = \tfrac12(e_{+} + e_{-})$, $v^{*} = \tfrac12(e_{+} - e_{-})$, with $v^{2} = v^{*2} = 0$ and $vv^{*} + v^{*}v = 1$, the pair the root paper adjoins and the tower paper reads as the one fermionic mode of the rung \cite[\S 2.2]{ButlerT1}, \cite[Prop.~4.1, Thm.~4.2]{ButlerT3}. The note's canonical frame is the same two null rays, $v = I_{0}$ and $v^{*} = \varphi/2$. Then: at $\Lambda = 0$ the frozen point is the null generator $v$ itself, the zero divisor of vector type, and the direction the completion adjoins is its partner $v^{*}$, canonical by Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.transport-constrains-frozen-point-only-through}(i); the Stelle-West vector does not exist there. For $\Lambda \neq 0$ the frozen point is a combination of both null generators,
\[
I_{\Lambda} \;=\; \alpha\, v + \beta\, v^{*}, \qquad Q(I_{\Lambda}) = \alpha\beta = \Lambda/3 ,
\]
and the Stelle-West vector is the same two components with the relative sign reversed,
\[
V \;\propto\; \alpha\, v - \beta\, v^{*}, \qquad Q(V) \propto -\alpha\beta ,
\]
orthogonal to $I_{\Lambda}$ and to the Lorentz frame. So $I$ and $V$ are the sum and difference of one pair of null components, which is why they form the signed basis up to scale and a boost (Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed}(i)); the sign of $\Lambda$ is the relative sign of $\alpha$ and $\beta$, de Sitter when they agree and anti-de Sitter when they differ, and the wall is either of them vanishing. The dilation acts as $v \mapsto tv$, $v^{*} \mapsto v^{*}/t$, an automorphism of the relation $vv^{*} + v^{*}v = 1$, and $\alpha\beta$ is its invariant (Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.boost-dilation-ratio-gauge}); in the frame of Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.transport-constrains-frozen-point-only-through}, $\alpha = a$ and $\beta = 2b$. In the tower paper's reading of $v$ and $v^{*}$ as the annihilation and creation operators of the rung's mode, the frozen point of a $\Lambda = 0$ universe is a pure annihilator and a nonzero $\Lambda$ is a creation component, the product of the two coefficients being $\Lambda/3$; this is what that reading says verbatim; only the vanishing of the creation component is invariant, its size being the dilation gauge, and the note attaches no claim to the reading. The script verifies the null pair, its normalisation, the identification with the canonical frame, and the norms and orthogonality of $\alpha v \pm \beta v^{*}$ on instances of both signs and zero.

title: two bits, compared
text: The root paper's Rule 2 leaves a sign free too, the square of the generator adjoined to a type-C obstruction, and records that the completed algebra forgets it. The sign left free here is of a different kind. The completed algebra, the rung $\Cl(2,4)$, forgets it in the same way; but the intermediate algebra of Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed} remembers it, the doubled $\Cl(1,4)$ against the complexified $\Cl(2,3)$, because the base $\Cl(1,3)$ is even-dimensional and exactly one of the two single extensions changes the parity of $q$ (Lemma \claimref{odd-extensions.volume-element-odd-dimension}). So the sign of $\Lambda$ is a geometric datum with an algebraic witness one level below the rung, and the witness is what the section ``The rung's even subalgebra is the anti-de Sitter algebra'' used to separate the oriented towers.

title: what the transport stance does and does not say about $\Lambda$
text: The programme reads a zero divisor as a signpost rather than a prohibition, and Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed}(iii) puts $\Lambda = 0$ on the wall. It is tempting to read the stance as saying that a universe does not sit on the wall, hence $\Lambda \neq 0$. Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.transport-constrains-frozen-point-only-through} is what the stance actually delivers: the transport off the wall is the passage from $\Cl(1,3;1)$ to the rung, which is the same rung for every $\Lambda$, and it says nothing about where in the rung's new plane the frozen point lies. The dark-energy paper's finding that the norm is a parameter of the laws under the action as written is the dynamical form of the same statement, and this note does not improve on it.

title: Two negative results
Two negative results
text: Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.transport-constrains-frozen-point-only-through}(iii) says the frozen point's two components in the canonical null frame are related by a symmetry of the completion. This section adds that the symmetry is a gauge symmetry of the dark-energy paper's action, so the components are unphysical and not merely symmetry-related; and it shows that the sign of $\Lambda$, though it acts differently on the two oriented towers, does not select which of them is the visible one.

title: The boost is the dilation; the ratio $b/a$ is gauge
proof: (i) $I\varphi = \tfrac12(e_{+} + e_{-})(e_{+} - e_{-}) = 1 - e_{+}e_{-}$, so $I \wedge \varphi = -e_{+}e_{-}$ and $B^{2} = -e_{+}^{2}e_{-}^{2} = +1$; a bivector of a plane commutes with vectors orthogonal to the plane and anticommutes with vectors in it (\claimref{std-algebra.orthogonal-anticommute}). (ii) $R = \cosh\theta + B\sinh\theta$ is the exponential of the bivector $\theta B$ (\claimref{std-algebra.bivector-exponential}), and $R\tilde R = \cosh^{2}\theta - \sinh^{2}\theta = 1$, $R$ fixes what commutes with $B$, and on the plane $RxR^{-1}$ is the hyperbolic rotation by $2\theta$, whose eigenvectors are the null directions with eigenvalues $e^{\pm 2\theta}$. (iii) is (ii) with Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.transport-constrains-frozen-point-only-through}(iii) and Fact \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation}. The script verifies (i) and (ii) with the rational rotor $\cosh\theta = 5/4$, $\sinh\theta = 3/4$ ($t = 4$): unit, fixing $e_{1}, \ldots, e_{4}$, scaling $I$ by $4$ and $\varphi$ by $1/4$, and carrying a frozen point along its hyperbola with $2ab$ preserved.

title: The two towers on one gravitational field
proof: The metric $g$ below is the derived metric $g(a,b) = \hb^{-1}(a) \cdot \hb^{-1}(b)$ of the gravitational field and $-g$ the mirror's reading of it; its Levi-Civita connection, Ricci tensor and scalar curvature are read from $\Omega$ and $\mathcal{R}$ by Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}(ii) and (iv). (i) The tractor bundle of a conformal class of signature $(p,q)$ carries a metric of signature $(p+1,q+1)$ (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point}), so the class $[-g]$ of signature $(3,1)$ has a tractor metric of signature $(4,2)$; in a scale $g$ the tractor metric is $2\sigma\rho + g^{-1}(\mu,\mu)$ and the scale tractor of $\sigma$ is $(\sigma, \nabla\sigma, -(\Delta\sigma + J\sigma)/n)$ with $J$ a multiple of the scalar curvature; under $g \mapsto -g$ the Levi-Civita connection and the Ricci tensor are unchanged while the inverse metric, the Laplacian and the scalar curvature change sign, so $\rho \mapsto -\rho$; the map $\Phi: (\sigma, \mu, \rho) \mapsto (\sigma, \mu, -\rho)$ from the tractor bundle of $[g]$ to that of $[-g]$ is scale-independent, intertwines the two tractor connections, carries the scale tractor of $g$ to that of $-g$, and satisfies $h_{-g}(\Phi X, \Phi X) = -h_{g}(X, X)$. Hence the mirror's frozen point has norm $-Q(I)$ and its $I^{\perp}$ has the reversed signature of ours: $(4,1)$ against $(1,4)$ and $(3,2)$ against $(2,3)$; the doubling or complexification is Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.four-extensions-oriented-pair}. (ii) Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.doubling-or-complexification}(iii): with $e_{5}^{2} = -1$ in $\Cl(1,4)$ and $e_{5}^{2} = +1$ in $\Cl(4,1)$ the products $e_{\mu}e_{5}$ square to $e_{\mu}^{2}$ and $-e_{\mu}^{2}$ respectively, which are both $(+,-,-,-)$ since the two Lorentz frames are reversed; a Clifford algebra is determined by such a presentation. That the copy theorem's inputs are spin-group objects is Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-copy-theorem-soldered-residue}. (iii) is Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.doubling-or-complexification}(i) and Remark \claimref{note.odd-extensions.added-axis-pseudoscalar}. In the closing clause, the unit vector along $V$ lies outside the soldered space by Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.belongs-tower}(i) and in the pure-gauge sector by Fact \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation}. The script verifies the signatures of the mirror's $I^{\perp}$ on the same rational instances, the two-by-two rule from the signs of $\omega^{2}$, the common presentation of the even subalgebras, and the squares and factorisations of $e_{5}$.

title: the one operator that sees the difference
text: An operator linear in $e_{5}$ alone, a term $\bar\psi e_{5}\psi$, is the one place the doubling would show: $e_{5}$ is the real pseudoscalar in one tower and the pseudoscalar times a central complex unit in the other, which in the physicists' notation is $\gamma_{5}$ against $i\gamma_{5}$, an anti-Hermitian against a Hermitian bilinear. But $e_{5}$ is the unit Stelle-West direction, unsoldered by Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.belongs-tower}(i) and pure gauge by Fact \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation}; so either a coupling to it can be physical, in which case Fact \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation} is being read too strongly in Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.boost-dilation-ratio-gauge}(iii), or it cannot, in which case the mirror sector is observationally identical to this one at every level the series reaches. The note takes the second reading, consistently with Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.boost-dilation-ratio-gauge}, and records the operator as the one place the first reading would show; the Hermiticity statement depends on a Dirac-representation convention the note does not fix.

title: The wall in the cosmological constant
The wall in the cosmological constant
text: Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed} gives a one-parameter family of intermediate algebras, nondegenerate for $\Lambda \neq 0$ and degenerate at $\Lambda = 0$. The sheaf paper has a theory of exactly such families: tame corank-one degenerations, their exceptional algebras, the residue of the metric at the wall, and a conservation law that says the degeneracy of a wall in spacetime can be displaced but never destroyed. This section runs that theory on the $\Lambda$ line. The family is a tame wall in the sheaf paper's sense, and the rung completes it on both sides, which the conservation law forbids for the completions it covers; the family lies in the case the conservation theorem's proof excludes by hypothesis, a complement whose signature switches across the wall, and that case is generic to any corank-one family of hyperplanes in a fixed nondegenerate space. The section's content is the identification of the dark-energy paper's frozen-point geometry with the sheaf paper's tame structure, and the placement of the $\Lambda$ family in that excluded case.

title: Imported: tame walls, the exceptional algebra, the residue, and conservation
text: A pair $(M,G)$, $G$ a smooth symmetric form on a bundle over $M$, is a tame corank-one degeneration if (T1) the degenerate locus $\Sigma$ is a smooth closed hypersurface, (T2) the corank is exactly one on $\Sigma$ with the radical lines a smooth line bundle spanned locally by $k$, and (T3) the dying eigenvalue crosses zero at nonzero speed along every transversal, invariantly: the section $\delta(k \otimes k) = dg_{k}|_{\Sigma}$ of $\operatorname{Hom}(L^{\otimes 2}, N^{*}\Sigma)$ is nowhere zero. The signatures on the two sides differ by one unit, $(p,q)$ where the dying eigenvalue is positive against $(p-1, q+1)$. Rescaling the dying direction by $t^{-1/2}$ along a transversal gives a continuous family of nondegenerate algebras through the wall whose special fibre, the exceptional algebra, is the Clifford algebra of the surviving form orthogonal to the rate of degeneration, of signature $(p,q)$ on the side approached. The inverse form has a canonical simple pole at the wall whose residue is $\delta^{-1}$, giving $N^{*}\Sigma \cong L^{\otimes 2}$: the dying line is a square root of the conormal bundle and the adjoined partner line a square root of the normal bundle. Conservation, absolute form: for a tame wall with both sides nonempty, any symmetric form on any bundle containing the original, standard outside a neighbourhood of the wall in the sense of being $G \perp K$ there with $K$ nondegenerate of the \emph{same} signature on both exterior regions, degenerates somewhere; the constancy of $\operatorname{sig} K$ across the wall is necessary, a completion allowed to switch $K$'s signature being able to match the two sides. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Hyp.~2.1, Lem.~2.2, Rem.~2.3, Prop.~6.1, Thm.~6.2, Thm.~5.1]{ButlerT4}.

title: The $\Lambda$ line is a tame wall
proof: (i) With $2ab = \Lambda/3$ (Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.transport-constrains-frozen-point-only-through}(ii)), $Q(w_{\Lambda}) = -2ab = -\Lambda/3$, $\ip{w_{\Lambda}}{I_{\Lambda}} = ab - ab = 0$, and both are orthogonal to the Lorentz frame; the Gram is block diagonal because $I_{0}$ and $\varphi$ are. The radical at $\Lambda = 0$ is spanned by $w_{0} = aI_{0}$. The crossing speed is $d(-\Lambda/3)/d\Lambda = -1/3 \neq 0$, so (T1) to (T3) of Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-tame-walls-exceptional-algebra-residue} hold. (ii) is the sign of $-\Lambda/3$ read against Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.four-extensions-oriented-pair}. (iii) $a = b = \sqrt{\Lambda/6}$. The script verifies the Gram, the corank at $\Lambda = 0$ only, the gauge independence of the dying eigenvalue, the exact slope $-1/3$ at six nonzero rational values of $\Lambda$, and the two signatures.

title: Exceptional algebra, residue, and the completion on both sides
proof: (i) $V$ is the multiple of $w_{\Lambda}$ with $Q(V) = -3/\Lambda$ (Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed}), and $w_{\Lambda}/\sqrt{|\Lambda|}$ has norm $\mp 1/3$, so it is $e_{V}/\sqrt 3$; the rescaled Gram's dying entry is $(-\Lambda/3)/t$ with $t = \mp\Lambda$, and the off-diagonal entries are zero for every $\Lambda$ by Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.line-tame-wall}(i), so the sheaf paper's limit is attained identically; the signatures are by inspection. (ii) The inverse Gram's dying entry is $-3/\Lambda$, so $\Lambda$ times it is $-3$; the sheaf paper's residue formula gives $\lim \Lambda\, G^{-1} = (1/T)\,w_{0} \otimes w_{0}$ with $T = -1/3$; and $Q(V) = -3/\Lambda$ is Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point}. The weight statement is the sheaf paper's reading of $L^{\otimes 2} \cong N^{*}\Sigma$, and $H^{2} = Q(I) = \Lambda/3$ is \cite[Fact~2.5]{ButlerT12} (\claimref{standard-model.imported-frozen-point-dictionary}), the form the Standard-Model paper uses for its $N = M_{P}/H$ \cite[Obs.~7.1]{ButlerT12}. (iii) The rung's metric has signature $(2,4)$ for every $\Lambda$; at $\Lambda = 0$ the five vectors of $I_{0}^{\perp}$ together with $I_{0}$ span only five dimensions, $I_{0}$ being the radical, and the sixth direction is $\varphi$ (Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.transport-constrains-frozen-point-only-through}(i)); for $\Lambda \neq 0$ the sixth direction is $I_{\Lambda}$; the rank count $5 + 1 = 6$ is the projective-to-conformal paper's $m + r$ (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-minimal-completion-degenerate-algebra-rule}). For the general model, $Q(u + \tfrac{t}{2}v) = t$, the complement is spanned by $u - \tfrac{t}{2}v$ of norm $-t$, and the total is the fixed $(p+1,q+1)$; the $\Lambda$ family is the case $u = I_{0}$, $v = \varphi$ with $\ip{I_{0}}{\varphi} = 1$ and $t = -\Lambda/3$ up to the gauge. (iv) $Q(I_{\Lambda}) = \Lambda/3$ changes sign at the wall; Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-tame-walls-exceptional-algebra-residue}'s conservation theorem requires $\operatorname{sig} K$ constant across it, and its proof states that the clause is necessary because a completion allowed to switch $K$'s signature can match the two sides, which is what happens here. The script verifies (i) to (iv) on the same rational instances: the rescaled dying entries, the two exceptional signatures, $\Lambda\,(G^{-1})_{ww} = -3$ for every $\Lambda \neq 0$, the total signature $(2,4)$ on both sides with the sign of $K$ switching, the five-dimensional span at $\Lambda = 0$, and the signature $(2,4)$ of the Lorentz frame with $I_{0}$ and $\varphi$.

title: Two classes of completion
text: The sheaf paper's conservation theorem concerns completions with one exterior model: the same nondegenerate complement $K$ on both sides of the wall. For those, degeneracy is conserved and displaced to a shadow wall, and the ambient adjoins a hyperbolic plane to the whole bundle: rank two by Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-minimal-completion-degenerate-algebra-rule}, and to the whole bundle because off the wall the bundle is nondegenerate and the standard complement must exist there. The $\Lambda$ family is completed by a construction of the other class: a family of hyperplanes in one fixed nondegenerate space, whose complement is a single line that changes type across the wall, rank one. Nothing prevents a spacetime wall from being completed in the second class as well, with a complement that is not standard; what the sheaf paper proves is that the first class cannot be made two-sided. The transport principle's founding move, resolving a nilpotent by a pair, is the first class, and the frozen point's passage from anti-de Sitter to de Sitter is the second, which is not a transport (Definition \claimref{obj.odd-extensions.single-extension}).
proof: Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.exceptional-algebra-residue-completion-both-sides}(iii) and (iv) against Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-tame-walls-exceptional-algebra-residue}. The rank two of the first class rests on Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-minimal-completion-degenerate-algebra-rule}, which supplies that a minimal completion of a radical of dimension $r$ adjoins exactly $2r$ dimensions, one hyperbolic plane for a corank-one wall.

title: what the section adds
text: That the family of intermediate algebras in $\Lambda$ is a tame wall at all is generic (Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.exceptional-algebra-residue-completion-both-sides}(iii)). What is specific to the cosmological constant is which objects of the dark-energy paper play the tame structure's roles: the frozen point's null direction is the radical, the Stelle-West line is the dying direction and the Stelle-West norm is the residue; the completion on both sides that the rung provides is the generic one for a family of hyperplanes and is recorded as an instance of the case the conservation theorem excludes, not as a property of $\Lambda$. None of this fixes $\Lambda$, its sign or its magnitude: the family is parametrised by $\Lambda$ and the theory describes the family.

title: What this note depends on
What this note depends on
text:
The note makes no prediction; no observation can refute its identifications, and the only observational input it uses is the sign of $\Lambda$, which selects which branch describes this universe (Remark \claimref{note.odd-extensions.what-says-what-it-does-not}). What it claims is a set of identifications, each proved in the note from imported results, and this section says which imported result each identification depends on and what falls with it.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(D1)] \emph{The frozen point.} Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed}, Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.translation-bivectors-frozen-point} and all of the section ``The soldering decides'', the section ``Running the transport on the wall'', the section ``Two negative results'' and the section ``The wall in the cosmological constant'' rest on the dark-energy paper's frozen point (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point}): the parallel scale tractor of norm $\Lambda/3$ with the Stelle-West vector as the fifth direction of $I^{\perp}$. Without it the algebra of the section ``The frozen point splits the ascent's pair'' is a statement about an arbitrary vector of the rung's hyperbolic plane with no physical referent.
\item[(D2)] \emph{The soldered residue.} Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.belongs-tower} and Corollaries \claimref{odd-extensions.two-readings-which-which} and \claimref{odd-extensions.not-coupling-between-towers} rest on the dark-matter paper's definition of the residue as the signature of the tangent image (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-copy-theorem-soldered-residue}). A definition admitting unsoldered directions into the residue would reopen both questions the section closes and, by the same stroke, the exactness of the dark-matter paper's superselection.
\item[(D3)] \emph{The copy theorem's inputs.} Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.copy-theorems-blind-spot} and Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.two-towers-one-curved-universe}(ii) rest on every input of the copy theorem being a spin-group object (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-copy-theorem-soldered-residue}), and Remark \claimref{note.odd-extensions.one-operator-sees-difference}'s conclusion that the mirror sector is observationally identical to this one rests on Fact \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation}: a derived quantity depending on the bare fifth generator would need a physical coupling to the pure-gauge direction, which that Fact excludes.
\item[(D4)] \emph{The Goldstone proposition.} Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.boost-dilation-ratio-gauge}(iii) rests on the dark-energy paper's $(I,V)$ sector being pure gauge (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation}); a dynamical fixing of the dilation gauge would make the ratio $b/a$ physical.
\item[(D5)] \emph{The residue of a conformal class.} Remark \claimref{note.odd-extensions.holographic-coincidence}'s statement that the boundary of $\mathrm{AdS}_{4}$ has residue $7$ and lies in a tower distinct from the bulk's rests on Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-conformal-completion}, on Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-towers-clock}, and on the signature of a conformal class being well defined. A definition of the residue requiring a chosen scale would withdraw it, and with it the remark's statement of the difference between the two frameworks.
\item[(D6)] \emph{The sheaf paper's hypotheses.} the section ``The wall in the cosmological constant'' rests on the sheaf paper's tameness conditions and conservation theorem as stated (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-tame-walls-exceptional-algebra-residue}); its one observation is about the hypothesis of that theorem and stands or falls with the theorem's statement.
\end{enumerate}
the section ``What a single generator does'' to the section ``The clock, and the paths between the oriented towers'' prove their algebra in the note, importing Facts \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-representatives-dimension-nearest-four-types} and \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-towers-clock} for it; their identifications with the frozen point, in Propositions \claimref{odd-extensions.translation-bivectors-frozen-point} and \claimref{odd-extensions.four-extensions-are-four-odd-towers}, rest on Facts \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-conformal-completion} and \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point} as (D1) records, and the copy theorem's inputs in Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.twistor-algebra}(iii), with the superselection read in Remarks \claimref{note.odd-extensions.what-says-what-it-does-not} and \claimref{note.odd-extensions.no-mechanism}, on Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-copy-theorem-soldered-residue}.

title: Position in the series
Position in the series
text: This paper is T14a of the series, a companion to the dark-matter paper T14 \cite{ButlerT14}, downstream of its Theorem 3.4 (types by residue), Theorem 3.5 (the soldered residue), Proposition 4.1 (superselection) and Theorem 4.3 (the mirror copy), and it says where that copy theorem stops: at the real form. It uses the tower paper T3 \cite{ButlerT3} for the clock, the transport paper T1 \cite{ButlerT1} for why a single generator is not a transport, the twistor paper T9 \cite{ButlerT9} and the Standard-Model paper T12 \cite{ButlerT12} for the conformal completion and the twistor module, and the dark-energy paper T10 \cite{ButlerT10} for the frozen point, whose rank-five bundle $I^{\perp}$ is the physical occurrence of the single extension. A sibling companion note to T14 constructs the odd-dimensional twistor spaces and the odd towers' content under the reading in which all five generators are soldered; this note is upstream of nothing there and is consistent with it, the two reading the same odd algebras under different solderings, which Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.belongs-tower} assigns to different towers. Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed} is downstream of T10's Theorem 3.1 and gives its parabolic-to-reductive rotation an algebraic form (Remark \claimref{note.odd-extensions.what-adds-dark-energy-paper}); Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.transport-constrains-frozen-point-only-through} runs the completion theorem of the projective-to-conformal paper T2 \cite{ButlerT2} on the wall of Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed}(iii) and finds the cosmological constant to be the one modulus the transport leaves free, which the capstone should record beside T10's parameter-of-the-laws finding; the section ``Two negative results'' adds that the frame's components are gauge by T10's Goldstone proposition and that the sign of $\Lambda$ does not select the visible tower. the section ``The wall in the cosmological constant'' runs the sheaf paper T4 \cite{ButlerT4} on the family over the $\Lambda$ line and finds it a tame wall completed in the class the conservation theorem excludes (Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.two-classes-completion}), which T4's successor-problem list should carry. The capstone T17 \cite{ButlerT17} should carry Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.copy-theorems-blind-spot} as the statement of what the copy theorem does and does not identify above the shadow, Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.cosmological-constant-deforms-wall} beside T10's entry, and Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.not-coupling-between-towers} beside the odd towers' missing coupling rule, which this note leaves as missing.

title: Machine verification
Machine verification
text:
Every computational identity asserted in this note has been verified in exact rational arithmetic by the script \texttt{verify\_T14a.py} \cite{ButlerVerifyT14ext}, which imports the series' shared library \texttt{GA.py} and uses its basis-blade engine; no floating point anywhere. The script indexes generators from zero, so its $e_{0}, \ldots, e_{5}$ are the text's $e_{1}, \ldots, e_{6}$. Eighty-six checks, all passing, in nine parts.

\emph{Part A: the volume element.} Centrality and the sign $\omega^{2} = (-1)^{n(n-1)/2+q}$ on every diagonal signature of dimensions one, three, five and seven; the four signs of Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.four-extensions-oriented-pair}; commutation of $\omega$ with the added generator; Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.doubling-or-complexification}(iii) and the identities behind (i) and (ii), with the specific sign assignment of (i), over every odd signature of dimensions three and five; and the dimension of the centre, two over every odd signature of dimension at most five and one over every even signature of dimension at most six.

\emph{Part B: doubling and complexification.} For the two doubled extensions, the central idempotents $(1 \pm \omega)/2$, the two ideals of dimension sixteen, the action of $e_{5}$ as $+s\,\omega'$ and $-s\,\omega'$ on them with $s = e_{5}^{2}$, and the shadow meeting the even subalgebra exactly in its even part; for the two complexified extensions, the spanning of all thirty-two dimensions by $\Cl(p,q) + \omega\,\Cl(p,q)$ and $\omega^{2} = -1$ central.

\emph{Part C: where the mirror sits.} For all four extensions, the pairwise anticommutation and the squares of the bivectors $e_{\mu}e_{5}$, the generated subalgebra equal to the even subalgebra, the shadow of dimension sixteen meeting it in dimension eight, and the squares of $\omega e_{\mu}$ (reversed in the complexified cases, unchanged in the doubled ones); for $\Cl(2,3)$, the intersection equal to $\Cl^{0}(1,3)$.

\emph{Part D: the rung.} In $\Cl(2,4)$, the signatures $(2,3)$ and $(4,1)$ generated by $e_{i}e_{6}$ and $e_{i}e_{1}$, both generating the even subalgebra of dimension thirty-two; $\omega_{6}$ even, $\omega_{6}^{2} = -1$, commuting with every even element and anticommuting with every vector; the copies of $\Cl(1,3)$ and $\Cl(3,1)$ inside the even subalgebra.

\emph{Part E: the clock and the paths.} The residues of the four extensions, of the oriented pair and of the odd towers' representatives; the residue preserved by conformal completion; the centres of the four extensions of dimension two with the signs that separate the reversed pairs, and the centre of the rung of dimension one; the enumeration of sign-change walks from $(1,3)$ to $(3,1)$, exactly one, with $(0,4)$ a dead end.

\emph{Part F: the frozen point and the ascent's pair.} On exact rational instances of $I = a\,e_{+} + b\,e_{-}$ with $Q(I) = 3$, $-3$ and $0$: the orthogonality of the Lorentz frame and $w$ to $I$, $Q(w) = -Q(I)$; the signatures $(1,4)$, $(2,3)$ and $(1,3;1)$ of $I^{\perp}$ by exact congruence; $w = I$ and $I^{2} = 0$ in the null case; the opposite signs and anticommutation of $I$ and $w$; the generation of all sixty-four dimensions by $I^{\perp}$ with $I$ when $Q(I) \neq 0$; in $\Cl(1,3;1)$ the nilpotent generator, its anticommutation with the Lorentz frame, the sixteen-dimensional ideal and its vanishing square; and the signature $(1,3)$ of the Lorentz frame in all three cases.

\emph{Part G: the transport on the wall.} In the projective-to-conformal paper's model of the completion of $(1,3;1)$: the signature $(2,4)$ by exact congruence; the rank-five linear system for the image of the partner and its unique null solution $c = 0$; the norm $2ab$ of $aI + b\varphi$ on instances of both signs and zero; the invariance of the norm under rational boosts and the swap, the image staying orthogonal to the Lorentz frame; the centres of the two intermediate algebras; and the null pair $v, v^{*}$ in the root paper's normalisation, its identification with the canonical frame, and the norms $\pm\alpha\beta$ and orthogonality of $\alpha v \pm \beta v^{*}$.

\emph{Part H: the two negative results.} The canonical null frame in the rung's diagonal basis; $B = I \wedge \varphi = -e_{+}e_{-}$ with $B^{2} = 1$, commuting with the Lorentz bivectors and vectors and anticommuting with $e_{\pm}$; the rational rotor $5/4 + (3/4)B$ unit, fixing the Lorentz frame, scaling $I$ by $4$ and $\varphi$ by $1/4$, moving a frozen point along its hyperbola; the mirror's $I^{\perp}$ signatures $(4,1)$ and $(3,2)$ on the same instances; the two-by-two rule; the common presentation of $\Cl^{0}(1,4)$ and $\Cl^{0}(4,1)$; and the squares and factorisations of the bare fifth generator.

\emph{Part I: the wall in the cosmological constant.} In four dilation gauges and at seven rational values of $\Lambda$ including zero: the Gram $\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1,-\Lambda/3)$ of $I_{\Lambda}^{\perp}$ and its corank at $\Lambda = 0$ only; the gauge independence of the dying eigenvalue; the exact crossing slope $-1/3$ in the parametrisation by $\Lambda$; the signatures $(2,3)$ and $(1,4)$ on the two sides; the rescaled dying entries $\pm 1/3$ and the exceptional signatures; $\Lambda\,(G^{-1})_{ww} = -3$ in every gauge with $w_{0} = a\,I_{0}$; the total signature $(2,4)$ on both sides with the complement's sign switching; the five-dimensional span at the wall and the signature of the Lorentz frame with $I_{0}$ and $\varphi$; and the general hyperplane model of Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.exceptional-algebra-residue-completion-both-sides}(iii) for five signatures $(p,q)$ and five values of $t$.

What the script does not check: the isomorphism types $\Mat(2,\HH)$ and $\Mat(4,\R)$ of the two oriented shadows (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-representatives-dimension-nearest-four-types}, imported; the note uses that they differ and, in Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.copy-theorems-blind-spot}, which type belongs to which tower), the frozen-point geometry (Facts \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point} and \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point-degenerate-algebras}, imported; the script checks the algebra of a vector of each norm sign in the rung, not that the parallel tractor is that vector), the algebra-map properties of Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.doubling-or-complexification}(i) and (ii) (argued in the text; the script checks the identities they rest on and the four extensions in detail), the identification of the MacDowell-Mansouri translation part with the bivectors $e_{\mu}e_{5}$ beyond the signs of their squares, the reversal of the tractor norm under $g \mapsto -g$ (Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.two-towers-one-curved-universe}(i), argued in the text; Part H checks its consequences from the reversed signature declared as input), and the transitivity of the boosts on each level set of the norm (Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.transport-constrains-frozen-point-only-through}(iii), argued in the text; Part G checks invariance under particular boosts).

title: The frozen point makes the Stelle-West vector
Imported: the frozen point and its geometry
The point at infinity has no physical fluctuation: the $(I,V)$-sector is pure gauge
text:
Take the functional in its three-argument form, $S[
abla, I, V] \sim Q(I)^{-1}\int\epsilon(I, V, F, F)$, with $
abla$ the tractor connection, on flat spacetime the $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field $\Omega_{T}$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection} (its curvature $F$ the field strength of $\Omega_{T}$), and $I$ and $V$ independent sections subject to the Stelle-West constraints $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$, $\ip{V}{I} = 0$, $Q(V) = -3/\Lambda$; Lemma \claimref{dark-energy.stelle-west-vector-frozen-point} exhibits $V = X - (3/\Lambda)I$ as the canonical solution of the constraints on the Einstein region, but inside the variational principle $V$ is a field, since the canonical tractor $X$ is a fixed section and a transformation acting on $
abla$ and $I$ alone is not a symmetry of a functional that contains $X$. Then: the constrained fluctuation space of $(I, V)$ has dimension $9$ (twelve components less three independent linearised constraints; it fibres over the five tangential directions of $I$ with four-dimensional affine fibres of $\delta V$, and is not a direct sum); the stabiliser of the pair $(I, V)$ in $SO(2,4)$ is the Lorentz group of $\{I,V\}^\perp$, of dimension six, so the broken generators number $15 - 6 = 9$; and the infinitesimal action $\xi \mapsto (\xi\cdot I, \xi\cdot V)$ of the broken generators onto the constrained fluctuation space is bijective. Unitary gauge $\delta I = \delta V = 0$ therefore exists and is complete: every fluctuation of the pair is a gauge transformation, the eaten Goldstone modes reappearing as the frame freedom of the soldering form (the physical frame $\hb^{-1}(a)$ of the gravitational field, up to rotation gauge), the Stelle-West mechanism read in reverse. In unitary gauge the second variation of the action has legs only on the connection: the graviton carries no $(\delta I, \delta V)$ polarisation. This closes open item (ii) of Remark \claimref{note.dark-energy.weakness-dimension-nonlinear-bound-open-items} within the action's own variational principle; the four-dimensional lift of the s-wave no-go is the task of Assembly \claimref{dark-energy.lift-inherits-no-go-steps-itemised}, not of this proposition. \emph{Level:} the counting, the bijectivity, and the invariance of the integrand $\epsilon(I,V,F,F)$ under the ambient group acting on all three arguments are proved outright below; that the functional so gauge-fixed is the MacDowell-Mansouri functional is Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(ii)-(iii), with its assembly-level clause.
