title: Projection: every tower's content dilutes as this one's
text: Read Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point} as the sourcing rule: the one metric is the four-dimensional one, a tower shares its three spatial directions and its time, and the tower's contribution to the metric's source is its energy per unit of the shared three-volume, its content taken homogeneous along every direction it has. Then, for a tower of any dimension, with the extra directions (if any) either co-expanding with the shared scale factor $a$ or static, and with a missing shared direction (the three-dimensional towers, which contain two of the three shared spatial directions) filled by a family of sheets, comoving in the background and displaced with the matter in perturbations (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.reduced-response-gravity-needs-supporting-stress}), one per unit of comoving length along the missing direction, the projected energy density of non-relativistic matter dilutes as $a^{-3}$ and that of radiation (the zero modes along any static extra direction) as $a^{-4}$, exactly as in this tower. No tower is diluted away or into prominence relative to this one.

title: The residue is a soldered invariant, not an algebraic one
Superselected, hence dark and exactly stable
text:
By Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point} and the acoustic programme (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-gravity-only-coupling}, the series' acoustic no-go, at its mixed level: within the s-wave current algebra, with the sphere step conditional on the Indifference premise and the thermal state on premise (Q)), matter in a neighbouring tower gravitates on this metric and does nothing else observable at first order: dark by structural necessity, at that level. Stability is then not suppressed but exact, in three steps, the first of which is proved given the sector decomposition of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.frozen-phase-operators}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The tower charge $r$ is superselected in the frozen phase: frozen-phase operators are built from the one soldering and preserve its signature (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.residue-soldered-invariant-not-algebraic-one}), so portal matrix elements between residues vanish identically away from walls.
\item The walls are unreachable: singular loci ascend within-tower, since the completion adjoins exactly $(1,1)$ and preserves the residue (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-eight-towers-mod-8-clock}), while the mod-8 shadow walls that separate residues are displaced successively away from the physical region, by the wall-sequence theorem of the sheaf paper \cite[\S5]{ButlerT4}, under that theorem's hypotheses (a compact base and good couplings at every stage), carried here.
\item Therefore the only inter-tower event in the universe's history is the descent itself: the towers communicated once, at the origin, and have been in absolute mutual darkness but for weight ever since. The singular locus of a black hole is an inter-tower event for energy, as it already was for weight, and never for the residue of any quantum: energy crosses at the wall, the residue does not (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}).
\end{enumerate}
One residue is flagged at observation level: dark-tower matter crossing this tower's horizons carries superselected charge the four-dimensional boundary mode space cannot hold, which routes it into the tower-wise run of the singularity paper's ascend-then-descend structure \cite{ButlerT5}; the computation of that routing, with the mass range of its Gauss-law clause, is Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}.

title: Towers are residues, and the single-clock filter
text:
The residue $r = p - q \pmod 8$ is invariant along every tower: the eight parallel towers are the eight residues, their parallelism derived rather than described. Call a signature $(p,q)$ \emph{causal} if $\min(p,q) = 1$: exactly one direction of the minority sign, the timelike one, whichever sign convention carries time. Labelling this world $(1,3)$, residue $6$, fixes the convention time $=$ plus, and the mirror residue $2$ reads $(3,1)$; under the opposite convention the two labels swap and the causal sort is unchanged, but every attribution of a Clifford type to a member of the reversal pair passes to the other member, since $\Cl(1,3) \cong \Mat(2,\mathbb{H})$ and $\Cl(3,1) \cong \Mat(4,\R)$ are not isomorphic. That attribution is fixed by a labelling convention Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference} declares indexical, and is so read below. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Census; proved.)} Every residue contains causal signatures once the dimension is free: the lowest are $(1,1)$ at $r = 0$, $(2,1)$ at $r = 1$, $(3,1)$ at $r = 2$, $(4,1)$ at $r = 3$, $(1,5)$ or $(5,1)$ at $r = 4$, $(1,4)$ at $r = 5$, $(1,3)$ at $r = 6$, $(1,2)$ at $r = 7$. The residue alone therefore sorts nothing; a representative must be chosen.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The sort under P3; proved given the premise.)} Under Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p3-nearest-dimension-representatives} the representatives are $(1,3)$ at $r = 6$, this world; $(3,1)$ at $r = 2$, a mirror Minkowski with real (Majorana-type) spinors; $(2,2)$ at $r = 0$, two times; $(4,0)$ or $(0,4)$ at $r = 4$, none; $(2,1)$ and $(1,2)$ at $r = 1, 7$, three-dimensional; $(4,1)$ and $(1,4)$ at $r = 3, 5$, five-dimensional. Exactly two are sterile, $r = 0$ and $r = 4$ (a figure of the original), and they are the fixed points of the mirror map $r \mapsto -r$: under P3 the towers without a single time are the towers that are their own mirrors.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Sensitivity; proved.)} The sterile set is a function of the window. With any dimension up to five allowed, only $r = 4$ is sterile ($(1,1)$ is a causal signature for $r = 0$); with dimensions three to six, only $r = 0$ ($(1,5)$ is one for $r = 4$); with the upper bound removed, nothing is ($(1,9)$ is one for $r = 0$ at ten); and the literal lowest-dimensional representative of every residue, with no lower bound, is definite for $r = 6$ itself, namely $(0,2)$: without a lower bound the criterion would sterilise this world.
\end{enumerate}
Six admit matter: this one and five dark. Which of the six the descent populated is a further question, answered for the mirror by P2 and for the odd towers only by the record (Observation \claimref{dark-matter.which-towers-are-populated}). Structural level given P3; the two-time exclusion at $r = 0$ imports the standard instability of two-time dynamics, flagged, and the flag does not remove it (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.flag-insensitive-residue-no-flag-level}).

The sign of $\omega^2$
text: $\displaystyle \omega^2 = (-1)^{\tfrac{n(n-1)}{2}} (-1)^q = (-1)^{\tfrac{(p-q)(p-q-1)}{2}}$. In particular $\omega^2 = +1$ if and only if $p - q \equiv 0$ or $1 \pmod 4$.

title: Conservation of degeneracy, absolute form
text: Let $M$ be connected, let $(M,G)$ be a tame corank-one degeneration whose two open sides $\Mp \setminus \Sig$ and $M \setminus \Mp$ are both nonempty, let $E \to M$ be \emph{any} vector bundle containing $T^*M$ as a subbundle, carrying \emph{any} smooth symmetric form $h$ which is \emph{standard} outside some neighbourhood $U$ of $\Sig$ with $M \setminus U$ meeting both sides: there, $h = G \perp K$ for a nondegenerate form $K$ on a complement, with $\operatorname{sig}(K)$ the same on both exterior regions. Then $h$ is not nondegenerate everywhere: every completion of a signature-change cometric that is standard, in this sense, outside a neighbourhood of the wall degenerates somewhere. Degeneracy can be displaced, never destroyed.

title: The degeneration sheaf
text:
Let $(M, G)$ be a tame corank-one degeneration (Hypotheses \claimref{sheaf.tameness}), $\shA = \Cl(T^*M, G)$, and write $A(x)$ for the fibre at $x$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Over $\Mo$, each fibre $A(x)$ is isomorphic to the nondegenerate Clifford algebra of the local signature; on the interior of $\Mp$ this is $\Cl(p,q)$, on the far side $\Cl(p{-}1,q{+}1)$. In the physical case these are $\Cl(1,3) \cong \Mat_2(\HH)$ and $\Cl(0,4) \cong \Mat_2(\HH)$.
\item Over $x \in \Sig$, the two-sided ideal $J(x)$ of $A(x)$ generated by the radical line $\shL(x)$ is
\[
J(x) \;=\; A(x)\,k \;=\; k\,A(x), \qquad J(x)^2 = 0, \qquad \dim_\R J(x) = 2^{n-1},
\]
for any spanning $k \in \shL(x)$, and the quotient is canonically the Clifford algebra of the induced form:
\[
A(x)/J(x) \;\cong\; \Cl\bigl(T^*_xM / \shL(x),\ \overline{G}_x\bigr),
\]
where $\overline{G}_x$ is nondegenerate of rank $n-1$ and signature $(p{-}1, q)$.
\item The fibrewise ideals assemble: the multiplication map $\shA|_\Sig \otimes \shL \to \shA|_\Sig$ has image a smooth subbundle $\shA|_\Sig \cdot \shL$ of rank $2^{n-1}$, and its pushforward
\[
\shJ \;:=\; i_*\bigl(\shA|_\Sig \cdot \shL\bigr) \qquad (i : \Sig \hookrightarrow M)
\]
is a finitely presented sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_M$-modules and of $\shA$-bimodules, supported exactly on $\Sig$, with fibre $J(x)$ at $x \in \Sig$ and fibre $0$ elsewhere. The associated ideal sheaf of $\shA$ is the kernel
\[
\shK \;:=\; \ker\bigl(\shA \longrightarrow i_*\bigl(\shA|_\Sig \,/\, \shA|_\Sig \cdot \shL\bigr)\bigr),
\]
a sheaf of two-sided ideals of $\shA$ whose restriction to $\Sig$ realises $J(x)$ fibrewise and whose quotient $\shA/\shK$ is the pushforward of the quotient bundle of (2).
\end{enumerate}

title: The exceptional algebra: deformation to the normal cone
text: Fix $x \in \Sig$ and a transversal curve through $x$ with parameter $t$, so that $G(t) = G_0 + t\dot G + O(t^2)$ with radical of $G_0$ spanned by $k$ and $\dot G(k,k) \neq 0$ by (T3). Rescale anisotropically: fix a complement $V_1$ of the radical and send $k \mapsto k/\sqrt{t}$. Then the rescaled forms converge as $t \to 0^+$ to the nondegenerate form $\hat G := G_0|_{V_1} \perp \dot G(k,k)$ on $V_1 \oplus \R k$: the cross terms are suppressed by $\sqrt{t}$, and the dying direction re-enters with its rate of degeneration as its metric coefficient. On the physical side the limit has signature $(p, q)$. The rescaled Clifford family is therefore a continuous family of nondegenerate algebras through $t = 0$, and its special fibre $\shE(x) := \Cl(V_1 \oplus \R k, \hat G)$, the \emph{exceptional algebra} at $x$, is independent of the choice of complement and of the scales of $k$ and $t$ up to canonical isomorphism.

title: The metric's residue, and the square-root twist
text:
At a tame wall the physical metric (the inverse cometric) has a canonical simple pole: for any defining function $\tau$ of $\Sig$,
\[
O \;:=\; \lim_{\tau \to 0}\, \tau\, G^{-1} \;=\; \frac{k \otimes k}{\delta(k \otimes k)/d\tau} ,
\]
a nowhere-vanishing section of $\shL \otimes \shL$ depending on $\tau$ through the weight of a section of $\shL \otimes \shL \otimes N\Sig$; invariantly, the residue is $\delta^{-1}$, the inverse of the transversality datum of Lemma \claimref{sheaf.invariant-form-t3}, regarded as a section of $\shL \otimes \shL \otimes N\Sig = \operatorname{Hom}(N^*\Sig, \shL^{\otimes 2})$. It is a nondegenerate pairing between $\shL^* \otimes \shL^*$ and $N^*\Sig$, hence induces a canonical isomorphism
\[
N^*\Sig \;\cong\; \shL^{\otimes 2} :
\]
the conormal bundle is the square of the dying direction itself. Dually, $N\Sig \cong (\shL^*)^{\otimes 2}$: the Witt partner line adjoined by the completion, which the pairing normalisation $kk^* + k^*k = 1$ identifies with $\shL^*$, is a canonical square root of the \emph{normal} bundle, and the dying line $\shL$ is a canonical square root of the conormal bundle. (The reading of the blow-up rescaling $k \mapsto k/\sqrt{t}$ as the normalisation of a conormal square root is Remark \claimref{note.sheaf.blow-up-dictionary}.)

title: One-sided completion
text: Assume (T1)-(T3), with signature $(p,q)$, $p \geq 1$, on the physical side $\Mp$, and assume the radical line bundle is trivial, $w_1(\shL) = 0$, so that collar data exist. Then there exists a smooth symmetric form $h$ on $T$ over $M$, equal to $G \perp H$ outside a collar of $\Sig$, which is nondegenerate of constant signature $(p{+}1, q{+}1)$ at every point of $\Mp$, including $\Sig$ itself. Consequently $\shC := \Cl(T, h)$ restricted to $\Mp$ is a locally free sheaf of algebras of constant rank $2^{n+2}$ whose every fibre is isomorphic to $\Cl(p{+}1, q{+}1)$; in the physical case, $\Cl(2,4) \cong \Mat_4(\HH)$.
provenance: Transport Lab claim sheaf.one-sided-completion, version 4 (T04 Thm 4.4)

title: Resolution, ideal-theoretically
text: Let $x \in \Sig$ and let $(\mathbb{W}, Q)$ be any nondegenerate quadratic space containing $(T^*_xM, G_x)$ as a subspace with the restricted form (a fibrewise completion, in the sense of the series). Then in $\Cl(\mathbb{W}, Q)$ the image of the radical line $\shL(x)$ generates the \emph{unit} ideal: the two-sided ideal generated by $k$ contains $1$. Resolution therefore converts a square-zero ideal into the unit ideal: it turns an infinitesimal into a dimension.

title: Imported: the Fock representation of a Clifford algebra, and its Bogoliubov group
text: Let $E$ be a complex vector space of dimension $n$ with a Hermitian inner product, and let $\Lambda^{\bullet}E$ be the Fock space of $n$ fermionic modes, with creation operators the exterior multiplications and annihilation operators the contractions. The $2n$ Majorana combinations of these operators generate an action of the complex Clifford algebra of a $2n$-dimensional orthogonal space on $\Lambda^{\bullet}E$, which is its irreducible spinor module; the parity grading $\Lambda^{\mathrm{even}} \oplus \Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}}$ is the chirality decomposition into the two half-spinor modules. The orthogonal transformations of the Majorana generators preserve the canonical anticommutation relations and are implemented on $\Lambda^{\bullet}E$ by the group $\mathrm{Pin}(2n)$, the connected component $SO(2n)$ by $\mathrm{Spin}(2n)$, which acts on each half-spinor module irreducibly for $n \ge 2$; the transformations preserving the complex structure of $E$, equivalently the mode number, form $U(n) \subset SO(2n)$, acting on $\Lambda^{\bullet}E$ as $\Lambda^{\bullet}(g)$ up to a determinant phase. For $n = 3$ this is the structure of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves}; for $n = 5$ it is $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$ with $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Lecture~20, \S 20.1]{FultonHarris1991} for the spinor module as an exterior algebra and its half-spin decomposition; \cite[Ch.~I, \S\S 2, 5]{LawsonMichelsohn1989} for $\mathrm{Spin}(2n)$ as the double cover of $SO(2n)$ and its spin representation; the Fock-space form is the standard second-quantised reading of the same construction.
provenance: W. Fulton and J. Harris, Representation Theory: A First Course, Graduate Texts in Mathematics 129, Springer (1991)., Lecture~20, \S 20.1; H. B. Lawson and M.-L. Michelsohn, Spin Geometry, Princeton University Press (1989)., Ch.~I, \S\S 2, 5

title: Imported: the frozen point and the dictionary
text:
On the Einstein region with $\Lambda \neq 0$ of a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), the frozen point $I$ is the scale tractor parallel for the tractor gauge field of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}, of squared norm $Q(I) = \Lambda/3 = H^{2}$, and in the flat chart of the conformal model (the flat twistor chart, the flat background itself) its frozen point is $I_{\Lambda} = n_{\infty} + (\Lambda/6)\,n_{0}$. Mass is conformal weight read against it: a density of weight $w$ coupled to the frozen point obeys the Klein-Gordon equation with
\[
m^{2} = -\,w(w+3)\,\frac{\Lambda}{3} = \Delta(3-\Delta)\,H^{2}, \qquad \Delta = -w,
\]
so a real weight gives $m^{2} \ge 0$ only on $w \in [-3, 0]$, where $m \le 3H/2$, and every heavier field has complex weight $w = -\tfrac32 \pm i\nu$ with $\nu \approx m/H$. In particular the weight of the Planck mass is complex, and its imaginary part is
\[
N := \operatorname{Im} w(M_{P}) \approx M_{P}/H, \qquad\text{about } 1.0 \times 10^{61}.
\]
Throughout this paper $N$ means $M_{P}/H$, the number the dictionary attaches to the Planck mass. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Thms.~4.5, 4.7]{ButlerT6} for the frozen point and its norm; \cite[Thm.~3.1, Cor.~3.2]{ButlerT11} for the dictionary and the complex weights; \cite[Lem.~5.1]{ButlerT11} for the chart form of $I_{\Lambda}$. The value, about $1.0 \times 10^{61}$ for $G = M_{P}^{-2}$, is the measured ratio $M_{P}/H$ and carries the record's status \cite{PDG2024}.

title: Exponentials of bivectors with scalar square
Orthogonal vectors anticommute
text: For $u, v \in V$: $u v = -v u$ if and only if $B(u, v) = 0$. In an orthogonal basis $e_1, \dots, e_n$, $e_i e_j = -e_j e_i$ for $i \ne j$ and $e_i^{2} = Q(e_i)$, and the product of two basis blades is $e_I e_J = \pm \bigl(\prod_{i \in I \cap J} Q(e_i)\bigr)\, e_{I \triangle J}$, the sign being $(-1)$ to the number of pairs $(i, j) \in I \times J$ with $i > j$.

title: The Pauli algebra: Cl(3,0) and 2 x 2 complex matrices
text: $\Cl(3,0) \cong \Mat_2(\C)$ by $e_k \mapsto \sigma_k$, where (as a labelled reading) $\sigma_1 = \begin{psmallmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{psmallmatrix}$, $\sigma_2 = \begin{psmallmatrix} 0 & -\mathrm{i} \\ \mathrm{i} & 0 \end{psmallmatrix}$, $\sigma_3 = \begin{psmallmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 \end{psmallmatrix}$ are the Pauli matrices. Under it the pseudoscalar $I = e_1 e_2 e_3$ goes to $\mathrm{i}\,1$: the centre $\R 1 \oplus \R I$ is a copy of $\C$, and the complex unit of the matrix reading is the pseudoscalar of space.

title: How the pseudoscalar commutes
The spacetime algebra as a matrix algebra, and the spacetime split
text: (i) $\Cl(1,3) \cong \Mat_2(\HH)$: with quaternion units $\mathbf{q}_1, \mathbf{q}_2, \mathbf{q}_3$, the assignment $\gamma_0 \mapsto \begin{psmallmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 \end{psmallmatrix}$, $\gamma_k \mapsto \begin{psmallmatrix} 0 & \mathbf{q}_k \\ \mathbf{q}_k & 0 \end{psmallmatrix}$ extends to an isomorphism. (ii) As a labelled reading, the Dirac matrices $\gamma^{D}_0 = \begin{psmallmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 \end{psmallmatrix}$, $\gamma^{D}_k = \begin{psmallmatrix} 0 & \sigma_k \\ -\sigma_k & 0 \end{psmallmatrix}$ ($2 \times 2$ blocks) give a faithful representation $\Cl(1,3) \to \Mat_4(\C)$ whose complex span is all of $\Mat_4(\C)$: $\C \otimes \Cl(1,3) \cong \Mat_4(\C)$. (iii) The relative vectors $\sigma_k = \gamma_k \gamma_0$ satisfy $\sigma_j \sigma_k + \sigma_k \sigma_j = 2\delta_{jk}$ and $\sigma_1 \sigma_2 \sigma_3 = I$, and generate the even subalgebra: $\Cl^{+}(1,3) \cong \Cl(3,0)$, so the spacetime pseudoscalar is the pseudoscalar of the observer's space.

title: The even subalgebra and the Z2 grading
text: $\Cl(V, Q) = \Cl^{+} \oplus \Cl^{-}$ with $\Cl^{i} \Cl^{j} \subseteq \Cl^{i+j}$ (indices mod $2$). So $\Cl^{+}$ is a subalgebra, of dimension $2^{n-1}$ for $n \ge 1$, and $\Cl^{-}$ is a $\Cl^{+}$-bimodule. More finely, $\Cl^{j}\Cl^{k} \subseteq \bigoplus_{m} \Cl^{|j-k| + 2m}$, $0 \le m \le \min(j,k)$.

title: Commuting copies
text:
Inside $T_k$, let $B_k$ be the subalgebra generated by the $2k$ plane generators $e_1, f_1, \dots, e_k, f_k$, and let $A_k$ be the subalgebra generated by the twisted base generators $x^{(k)} := x\,\omega_1 \omega_2 \cdots \omega_k$ for $x$ among the ground generators. Then: $B_k \cong \Cl(k,k) \cong \Mat_{2^k}(\R)$; $A_k \cong \Cl(p,q)$ via $x \mapsto x^{(k)}$ (the twisted generators satisfy the ground Clifford relations); $A_k$ and $B_k$ commute elementwise; and multiplication $A_k \otimes B_k \to T_k$ is an isomorphism of algebras,
\[
\Cl(p{+}k, q{+}k) \;\cong\; \Cl(p,q) \otimes \Mat_{2^k}(\R) \;=\; \Mat_{2^k}(\Cl(p,q)).
\]
The isomorphism is canonical given the ordered planes, and compatible with the tower embeddings up to the twist tracked in the section ``The CAR limit''.

title: Rigidity; the clock is frozen
text: Along the tower: the transport charge $d = p - q \bmod 8$ is constant; the division-ring type, simplicity class, and centre of every floor equal those of the ground floor; every floor is Morita equivalent to the ground floor; and the obstruction taxonomy of \cite{ButlerT1} is floor-independent: in particular a type-C obstruction (a central idempotent) never arises by transport from a simple ground algebra, at any height. The physical tower is $\Cl(1{+}k, 3{+}k) \cong \Mat_{2^{k+1}}(\HH)$, frozen at clock position $6$. Bott periodicity manifests as immediate freeze, not eventual return.
provenance: Transport Lab claim tower.rigidity-clock-frozen, version 5 (T03 Thm 3.6)

title: Minimality
text:
Let $(\mathbb{W}, f)$ be any null-lift completion of $(\mathbb{V}, Q)$. Then $\mathbb{W}$ contains at least one direction of positive square and one of negative square; in particular $\dim \mathbb{W} \geq 2$, and enlargements of signature increment $(+k, 0)$ or $(0, +k)$ are excluded for every $k$. A single hyperbolic plane suffices, and any two-dimensional $\mathbb{W}$ admitted by the definition is a hyperbolic plane; hence the minimal completion is
\[
\Cl(p,q) \;\longrightarrow\; \Cl(p{+}1, q{+}1),
\]
with the adjoined space unique up to isometry, and the signature increment is $(+1,+1)$ in every signature.
provenance: Transport Lab claim transport.minimality, version 4 (T01 Thm 4.13)

title: One generator is minimal; the minimal completions classified
text:
Let $A = \Cl(p,q)$, $p - q \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, and consider the Clifford algebras $\Cl(\mathbb{V}', Q')$ of arbitrary extensions $(\mathbb{V}', Q') \supseteq (\mathbb{V}, Q)$ of the quadratic space, $Q'$ possibly degenerate, each containing $A$ canonically and unitally. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\dim \mathbb{V}' = n$ (no ascent): $A$ itself is not simple (Theorem \claimref{transport.existence-classification-type-c}).
\item $\dim \mathbb{V}' = n + 1$, adjoined generator null ($\gamma = 0$): the fusion fails structurally. The subspace $J = A\nu$ is a nonzero proper two-sided ideal of $B_0$ with $J^2 = 0$, and $B_0 / J \cong A$: the degenerate ascent is an infinitesimal thickening of $A$, not a completion of it. (This square-zero ideal is the fibre-level germ of the degeneration sheaf of the series' sheaf-theoretic paper \cite{ButlerT4}.)
\item $\dim \mathbb{V}' = n + 1$, adjoined generator nondegenerate ($\gamma = \pm 1$ after rescaling): both ascents are simple and $\cong \Mat_2(\Cl^0(p,q))$ (Theorem \claimref{transport.rule-2-ideal-fusion-sharp-form}).
\item $\dim \mathbb{V}' \geq n + 2$: $\dim \Cl(\mathbb{V}') \geq 2^{n+2}$.
\end{enumerate}
Hence the minimal simple Clifford completions of $A$ are exactly the two one-generator ascents $\Cl(p{+}1,q)$ and $\Cl(p,q{+}1)$, of dimension $2^{n+1}$; they are inequivalent as quadratic data (the extensions $\langle +1 \rangle$ and $\langle -1 \rangle$ are non-isometric) but isomorphic as algebras; and so the minimal completion of a type-C obstruction is \emph{unique up to isomorphism}, with the residual geometric choice, the sign of the adjoined direction's square, not detected by the completed algebra.

title: The two one-generator ascents differ as algebras
text:
Refuted. The conjecture was that the two one-generator ascents of a type-C algebra, adjoining $
u$ with $Q(
u) = +1$ or with $Q(
u) = -1$, are non-isomorphic algebras. The corrected statement is that the two ascents are always isomorphic as algebras; the sign of $Q(
u)$ is a geometric bit that the algebra forgets.

title: Direct detection stays null
text: Permanent direct-detection nulls: dark matter couples through gravity alone, at first order.

title: No indirect dark-sector signals
text: No indirect dark-sector signals: no decay products, since the tower charge is superselected, and annihilation products only at the rate of graviton exchange, suppressed by powers of $E/M_{P}$ on a charge-asymmetric relic.
